concerns.location: plan.md:§ Implementation Plan – paragraph describing Wilcoxon tests (lines 31‑34)
concerns.text: The plan conducts Wilcoxon signed‑rank tests on F1‑scores across only five random seeds and then applies Benjamini‑Hochberg correction to seven comparisons. With n=5 paired observations the smallest two‑sided p‑value is ≈0.0625, so the declared significance threshold (BH‑adjusted p < 0.05) is unattainable, making the statistical inference invalid.

The deterministic ≤5 000‑node subsampling rule *always* retains all anomalous nodes and the top‑10 % highest‑degree nodes before random sampling. This preferential retention can bias the graph topology toward anomalies, inflating the GCN’s ability to detect them and confounding the comparison with baselines.

During temporal hold‑out, test‑set flows that involve IPs not present in the training graph are simply dropped. Dropping unseen nodes (which may include anomalous IPs) can systematically alter the class distribution in the test set, leading to optimistic precision/recall estimates.

The entire experimental pipeline is evaluated on a single verified dataset (NF‑BoT‑IoT‑v3). Claiming that GNNs “improve anomaly detection” without any external validation limits causal inference to this dataset and risks overgeneralization.

Phase 0 (Data Acquisition) is listed as a separate phase but no Functional Requirement (FR) or Success Criterion (SC) from the spec is explicitly mapped to it. The spec’s FR‑001 already covers dataset download/ingestion, so this extra phase is over‑reaching without a traceable requirement.

Phase 8 (Validation & Cleanup) addresses constitution principles (I, III, VII) but no FR or SC from the spec. While useful for reproducibility, it is not linked to any spec‑defined requirement, constituting an un‑anchored plan element.

The plan states it will ingest verified NetFlow records from the **NF‑BoT‑IoT‑v3** dataset (see line "ingest verified NetFlow records from the **NF‑BoT‑IoT‑v3** dataset"). However, the functional requirement **FR‑001** explicitly mandates ingestion of NetFlow records from the **CTU‑13** dataset. Substituting NF‑BoT‑IoT‑v3 changes the data domain (different traffic patterns, labeling schema) and therefore the experiment will not answer the research question as originally specified. This constitutes a wrong‑dataset issue that makes the methodology unable to satisfy the spec’s FR‑001.

The plan states that the pipeline will ingest the **NF‑BoT‑IoT‑v3** dataset, but **FR‑001** in the specification (spec.md) requires ingestion of the **CTU‑13** dataset. This violates the functional requirement and creates a mismatch between the plan and the spec.

The plan does not include an explicit step that validates the constructed graph against the **graph.schema.yaml** contract (e.g., a schema‑validation script). While graph construction is described, there is no mention of exercising the graph contract, which the constitution expects each contract to be exercised by at least one plan element.

The plan proposes Wilcoxon signed‑rank tests on F1‑scores across only five random seeds (FR‑006). With n = 5 paired observations the smallest attainable two‑sided p‑value is ≈0.0625, which can never meet the declared FDR < 0.05 threshold after Benjamini‑Hochberg correction (SC‑003). This makes the statistical significance claim untestable given the current sample size.

Node‑level anomaly labels are defined as “1 if the IP appears in any anomalous flow within the scenario” (research.md & data‑model.md). The plan does not restrict this aggregation to the training portion of the temporal hold‑out split, risking leakage of test‑set information into the training labels. If test‑set flows contribute to node labels, the evaluation metrics (Precision, Recall, F1, AUC) are no longer independent of the predictors, violating proper validation practice.

The entire experimental pipeline is evaluated on a single verified dataset (NF‑BoT‑IoT‑v3). Claiming that GNNs “improve anomaly detection” without any external validation limits causal inference to this dataset and risks overgeneralization.

new_concerns.text: Unseen IPs are added as isolated nodes with label 0 **and excluded from metric aggregation**. Excluding these nodes from the evaluation can bias precision/recall/F1 estimates because negative examples are omitted, potentially inflating performance. The methodology should either include them in the metric calculation or justify their exclusion.

new_concerns.text: The statistical analysis relies on Wilcoxon signed‑rank tests over only 5 random seeds, yielding a minimum attainable two‑sided p‑value of ≈0.0625. This makes it impossible to achieve the required FDR < 0.05 after Benjamini‑Hochberg correction (SC‑003), so the study cannot reliably demonstrate a statistically significant improvement of GNNs over baselines.
